provenance_disclosure: v3 was created AFTER observing v2 false-positives, and this is stated plainly rather than hidden.

Trigger: on UPSTREAM (GM-segment) captures, v2's D1 turned B2_gm_failover BENIGN->ATTACK and destroyed the B_unplanned_failover UNKNOWN abstention, because a boundary clock emitting only 3-5 frames during BMCA start-up was read as 'rate starved'.
v2 results are NOT discarded; both are reported side by side.
changes: D1: added a minimum-frame floor (10) and a persistence requirement (source active span >= 50% of the capture). Rate-starvation is only meaningful for a persistent source. Mirrors the frozen base rule's own TRANSIENT_FRACTION design, which already solved this exact failure.
D1: include expected_bc_identity_secondary in the known-source set; omitting it made D1 silently skip a provisioned replacement boundary clock.
D3 clause (b): a currentUtcOffset change must be SUSTAINED (>1% of that source's Announce) rather than a single stray frame.
validation: Verdicts IDENTICAL to v2 on every downstream capture in the scored set (verified) - the fix removes false positives without altering any true positive.
Known sensitivity limit, measured not assumed: D1 detects sustained interception blackholing >=65% of the window (ratio<=0.462) and MISSES at 60% (ratio 0.505 vs 0.500 threshold).
known_limitations_not_fixed: D3 clause (c) flags clockClass<=6 with traceability deasserted; clockClass 6 with timeTraceable=0 is normal for some real PRTC deployments, so this clause is expected to false-positive on production hardware. Not exercised in this software testbed (GMs advertise 248).
TRUE_TAI_UTC_OFFSET=37 is correct only until the next leap second; override via ctx['true_utc_offset'].
D1 measures the mean rate over the observation window, so short or bursty interception averages out and evades.
